source.text: וְאֵ֛לֶּה רָאשֵׁ֥י אֲבֹתֵיהֶ֖ם וְהִתְיַחְשָׂ֑ם הָעֹלִ֣ים עִמִּ֗י בְּמַלְכ֛וּת אַרְתַּחְשַׁ֥סְתְּא הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מִבָּבֶֽל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And these [are] the heads of their fathers and their genealogical enrollment, those going up with me in [the] reign of Artaxerxes the king from Babylon:

en.L: And these are the heads of their fathers' [houses], and their genealogical enrollment, those who went up with me from Babylon in the reign of Artaxerxes the king:
en.B: These are the heads of the ancestral families, with their genealogical records, who came up with me from Babylon during the reign of King Artaxerxes:
en.R: Here is a list of the family leaders who came with me from Babylon when Artaxerxes was king, and the families registered with them:

decisions.choice: the heads of their fathers: the heads of the ancestral families
decisions.reason: The phrase is short for "heads of their fathers' houses", the leaders of the extended families into which Israel's clans were divided (2:68; Numbers 1:2).

decisions.choice: their genealogical enrollment: the register of who belonged to each family
decisions.reason: Families proved their place in Israel by written descent (2:62). The list that follows names two priestly families, one royal family and twelve lay families, with about 1,500 men; women and children are not counted (8:21).

decisions.choice: heads of the ancestral families (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Balanced supplies what "fathers" stands for, as the book does elsewhere; Literal brackets the missing "houses".

source.text: מִבְּנֵ֤י פִֽינְחָס֙ גֵּֽרְשֹׁ֔םסמִבְּנֵ֥י אִיתָמָ֖ר דָּנִיֵּ֑אלסמִבְּנֵ֥י דָוִ֖יד חַטּֽוּשׁ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Of [the] sons of Phinehas, Gershom; of [the] sons of Ithamar, Daniel; of [the] sons of David, Hattush,

en.L: Of the sons of Phinehas, Gershom; of the sons of Ithamar, Daniel; of the sons of David, Hattush,
en.B: Of the descendants of Phinehas, Gershom; of the descendants of Ithamar, Daniel; of the descendants of David, Hattush,
en.R: Gershom, from the family of Phinehas; Daniel, from the family of Ithamar; Hattush, from the family of David,

decisions.choice: Phinehas, Ithamar, David: two priestly lines and the royal line
decisions.reason: Phinehas was Aaron's grandson through Eleazar, and Ithamar was Aaron's younger son (Exodus 6:23, 25; 1 Chronicles 24:1-4): the two branches of the priesthood. Hattush belonged to David's royal line (1 Chronicles 3:22). Gershom and Daniel lead their families; no numbers are given for them.

source.text: מִבְּנֵ֣י שְׁכַנְיָ֔הסמִבְּנֵ֥י פַרְעֹ֖שׁ זְכַרְיָ֑ה וְעִמּ֛וֹ הִתְיַחֵ֥שׂ לִזְכָרִ֖ים מֵאָ֥ה וַחֲמִשִּֽׁים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: of [the] sons of Shecaniah; of [the] sons of Parosh, Zechariah, and with him enrolled of males one hundred and fifty.

en.L: of the sons of Shecaniah. Of the sons of Parosh, Zechariah, and with him were enrolled 150 males.
en.B: of the descendants of Shecaniah. Of the descendants of Parosh, Zechariah, and with him 150 men were registered.
en.R: a descendant of Shecaniah. Zechariah, from the family of Parosh, and 150 men listed with him.

decisions.choice: of the sons of Shecaniah belongs with Hattush in verse 2
alternatives: a separate entry: Of the sons of Shecaniah, of the sons of Parosh, Zechariah
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 3:22 names Hattush among the descendants of Shecaniah in David's line. So the phrase most likely ends the entry for Hattush, and the next entry begins with Parosh, following the pattern of verses 3-14. The verse division places it here.

decisions.choice: enrolled males: men and boys counted in the register
decisions.reason: The verb means to be entered in a genealogy. The word for the people counted is "males"; it probably counts the men of each family, perhaps with the boys.

decisions.choice: men (Balanced, Readable); males (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the natural word for the people counted; Literal keeps "males". The same choice runs through verses 3-14.

source.text: מִבְּנֵי֙ פַּחַ֣ת מוֹאָ֔ב אֶלְיְהֽוֹעֵינַ֖י בֶּן־זְרַֽחְיָ֑ה וְעִמּ֖וֹ מָאתַ֥יִם הַזְּכָרִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Of [the] sons of Pahath-moab, Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred the males.

en.L: Of the sons of Pahath-moab, Eliehoenai the son of Zerahiah, and with him 200 males.
en.B: Of the descendants of Pahath-moab, Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah, and with him 200 men.
en.R: Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah, from the family of Pahath-moab, and 200 men with him.

decisions.choice: Pahath-moab: a family that had returned with the first group
decisions.reason: Most of the family names in verses 3-14 also appear in the list of the first return (2:3-15), so these men joined relatives already in Judah. Pahath-moab means "governor of Moab".

source.text: מִבְּנֵ֥י שְׁכַנְיָ֖ה בֶּן־יַחֲזִיאֵ֑ל וְעִמּ֕וֹ שְׁלֹ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת הַזְּכָרִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Of [the] sons of Shecaniah, son of Jahaziel, and with him three hundred the males.

en.L: Of the sons of Shecaniah, the son of Jahaziel, and with him 300 males.
en.B: Of the descendants of Shecaniah, the son of Jahaziel, and with him 300 men.
en.R: The son of Jahaziel, from the family of Shecaniah, and 300 men with him.

decisions.choice: a family name seems to be missing
alternatives: Of the descendants of Zattu, Shecaniah son of Jahaziel
decisions.reason: Every other entry names a family and then its leader. Here the Hebrew text has "of the sons of Shecaniah, son of Jahaziel". The Greek translation reads "of the sons of Zattu, Shecaniah son of Jahaziel", which fits the pattern and the list of 2:8. The Hebrew text is translated as it stands.

source.text: וּמִבְּנֵ֣י עָדִ֔ין עֶ֖בֶד בֶּן־יוֹנָתָ֑ן וְעִמּ֖וֹ חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים הַזְּכָרִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And of [the] sons of Adin, Ebed son of Jonathan, and with him fifty the males.

en.L: And of the sons of Adin, Ebed the son of Jonathan, and with him fifty males.
en.B: Of the descendants of Adin, Ebed son of Jonathan, and with him fifty men.
en.R: Ebed son of Jonathan, from the family of Adin, and fifty men with him.

source.text: וּמִבְּנֵ֣י עֵילָ֔ם יְשַֽׁעְיָ֖ה בֶּן־עֲתַלְיָ֑ה וְעִמּ֖וֹ שִׁבְעִ֥ים הַזְּכָרִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And of [the] sons of Elam, Jeshaiah son of Athaliah, and with him seventy the males.

en.L: And of the sons of Elam, Jeshaiah the son of Athaliah, and with him seventy males.
en.B: Of the descendants of Elam, Jeshaiah son of Athaliah, and with him seventy men.
en.R: Jeshaiah son of Athaliah, from the family of Elam, and seventy men with him.

decisions.choice: Athaliah: here a man's name
decisions.reason: The name, borne by the queen of 2 Kings 11, is here the name of Jeshaiah's father; it is also a man's name in 1 Chronicles 8:26.

source.text: וּמִבְּנֵ֣י שְׁפַטְיָ֔ה זְבַדְיָ֖ה בֶּן־מִֽיכָאֵ֑ל וְעִמּ֖וֹ שְׁמֹנִ֥ים הַזְּכָרִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And of [the] sons of Shephatiah, Zebadiah son of Michael, and with him eighty the males.

en.L: And of the sons of Shephatiah, Zebadiah the son of Michael, and with him eighty males.
en.B: Of the descendants of Shephatiah, Zebadiah son of Michael, and with him eighty men.
en.R: Zebadiah son of Michael, from the family of Shephatiah, and eighty men with him.

source.text: מִבְּנֵ֣י יוֹאָ֔ב עֹבַדְיָ֖ה בֶּן־יְחִיאֵ֑ל וְעִמּ֕וֹ מָאתַ֛יִם וּשְׁמֹנָ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר הַזְּכָרִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Of [the] sons of Joab, Obadiah son of Jehiel, and with him two hundred and eighteen the males.

en.L: Of the sons of Joab, Obadiah the son of Jehiel, and with him 218 males.
en.B: Of the descendants of Joab, Obadiah son of Jehiel, and with him 218 men.
en.R: Obadiah son of Jehiel, from the family of Joab, and 218 men with him.

source.text: וּמִבְּנֵ֥י שְׁלוֹמִ֖ית בֶּן־יוֹסִפְיָ֑ה וְעִמּ֕וֹ מֵאָ֥ה וְשִׁשִּׁ֖ים הַזְּכָרִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And of [the] sons of Shelomith, son of Josiphiah, and with him one hundred and sixty the males.

en.L: And of the sons of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah, and with him 160 males.
en.B: Of the descendants of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah, and with him 160 men.
en.R: The son of Josiphiah, from the family of Shelomith, and 160 men with him.

decisions.choice: a family name seems to be missing, as in verse 5
alternatives: Of the descendants of Bani, Shelomith son of Josiphiah
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "of the sons of Shelomith, son of Josiphiah". The Greek translation reads "of the sons of Bani, Shelomith son of Josiphiah", which fits the pattern of the list and the family of Bani in 2:10. The Hebrew text is translated as it stands.

source.text: וּמִבְּנֵ֣י בֵבַ֔י זְכַרְיָ֖ה בֶּן־בֵּבָ֑י וְעִמּ֕וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וּשְׁמֹנָ֖ה הַזְּכָרִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And of [the] sons of Bebai, Zechariah son of Bebai, and with him twenty-eight the males.

en.L: And of the sons of Bebai, Zechariah the son of Bebai, and with him twenty-eight males.
en.B: Of the descendants of Bebai, Zechariah son of Bebai, and with him twenty-eight men.
en.R: Zechariah son of Bebai, from the family of Bebai, and twenty-eight men with him.

source.text: וּמִבְּנֵ֣י עַזְגָּ֔ד יוֹחָנָ֖ן בֶּן־הַקָּטָ֑ן וְעִמּ֕וֹ מֵאָ֥ה וַעֲשָׂרָ֖ה הַזְּכָרִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And of [the] sons of Azgad, Johanan son of Hakkatan, and with him one hundred and ten the males.

en.L: And of the sons of Azgad, Johanan the son of Hakkatan, and with him 110 males.
en.B: Of the descendants of Azgad, Johanan son of Hakkatan, and with him 110 men.
en.R: Johanan son of Hakkatan, from the family of Azgad, and 110 men with him.

decisions.choice: Hakkatan: a name meaning "the small one"
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary adjective "small" with the article. It is taken as a name, the father of Johanan; it could also describe Johanan as "the younger".

source.text: וּמִבְּנֵ֣י אֲדֹנִיקָם֮ אַחֲרֹנִים֒ וְאֵ֣לֶּה שְׁמוֹתָ֔ם אֱלִיפֶ֖לֶט יְעִיאֵ֣ל וּֽשְׁמַעְיָ֑ה וְעִמָּהֶ֖ם שִׁשִּׁ֥ים הַזְּכָרִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And of [the] sons of Adonikam, last ones, and these [are] their names: Eliphelet, Jeiel and Shemaiah, and with them sixty the males.

en.L: And of the sons of Adonikam, the last ones, and these are their names: Eliphelet, Jeiel and Shemaiah, and with them sixty males.
en.B: Of the descendants of Adonikam, the last ones, whose names were Eliphelet, Jeiel and Shemaiah, and with them sixty men.
en.R: Eliphelet, Jeiel and Shemaiah, the last members of the family of Adonikam, and sixty men with them.

decisions.choice: the last ones: the last of the family to return
decisions.reason: The word means "last" or "latest". Most of Adonikam's family had returned with the first group (2:13), so these were likely the last of them to come. It could also mean the younger sons of the family.

source.text: וּמִבְּנֵ֥י בִגְוַ֖י עוּתַ֣י וְזַכּ֑וּר וְעִמּ֖וֹ שִׁבְעִ֥ים הַזְּכָרִֽים׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And of [the] sons of Bigvai, Uthai and Zaccur, and with him seventy the males.

en.L: And of the sons of Bigvai, Uthai and Zaccur, and with him seventy males.
en.B: Of the descendants of Bigvai, Uthai and Zaccur, and with them seventy men.
en.R: Uthai and Zaccur, from the family of Bigvai, and seventy men with them.

decisions.choice: Zaccur: the reading the Hebrew margin gives
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text spell Zabbud; the traditional reading marked for them is Zaccur. The translation follows the reading.

decisions.choice: with them (Balanced, Readable); with him (Literal)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "with him" after two names, perhaps thinking of the first; Balanced and Readable say "them" so the sentence reads naturally.

source.text: וָֽאֶקְבְּצֵ֗ם אֶל־הַנָּהָר֙ הַבָּ֣א אֶֽל־אַהֲוָ֔א וַנַּחֲנֶ֥ה שָׁ֖ם יָמִ֣ים שְׁלֹשָׁ֑ה וָאָבִ֤ינָה בָעָם֙ וּבַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים וּמִבְּנֵ֥י לֵוִ֖י לֹא־מָצָ֥אתִי שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I gathered them to the river that goes to Ahava, and we camped there three days; and I considered the people and the priests, and of [the] sons of Levi not I found there.

en.L: And I gathered them at the river that runs to Ahava, and we camped there three days. And I looked over the people and the priests, and I found none of the sons of Levi there.
en.B: I assembled them at the canal that flows toward Ahava, and we camped there for three days. When I reviewed the people and the priests, I found no Levites there.
en.R: I gathered them all by the canal that flows toward Ahava, and we camped there for three days. I checked over the people and the priests, and I found that there were no Levites among them.

decisions.choice: the river that goes to Ahava: a canal or stream near Babylon
decisions.reason: Ahava is the name of a place and of the waterway by it (verses 21, 31). Its site is not known; it was the gathering point before the journey, and the company stayed there from the first to the twelfth of the first month (7:9; 8:31). The word for river is also used of Babylon's canals (Psalm 137:1).

decisions.choice: no Levites: none of the Levites had come forward
decisions.reason: Few Levites had returned with the first group either: seventy-four, against more than four thousand priests (2:36-40). Their work was humbler than the priests', and many had settled in Babylonia. Ezra needed them to carry the holy objects and serve in the temple (Numbers 3-4).

decisions.choice: canal (Balanced, Readable); river (Literal)
decisions.reason: The waterways around Babylon were mostly canals, and Ahava was not a great river; Balanced and Readable say "canal". Literal keeps "river".

decisions.choice: Levites (Balanced, Readable); sons of Levi (Literal)
decisions.reason: "Sons of Levi" means the members of the tribe of Levi, the Levites.

source.text: וָאֶשְׁלְחָ֡ה לֶאֱלִיעֶ֡זֶר לַאֲרִיאֵ֡ל לִֽ֠שְׁמַעְיָה וּלְאֶלְנָתָ֨ן וּלְיָרִ֜יב וּלְאֶלְנָתָ֧ן וּלְנָתָ֛ן וְלִזְכַרְיָ֥ה וְלִמְשֻׁלָּ֖ם רָאשִׁ֑ים וּלְיוֹיָרִ֥יב וּלְאֶלְנָתָ֖ן מְבִינִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And I sent for Eliezer, for Ariel, for Shemaiah, and for Elnathan and for Jarib and for Elnathan and for Nathan and for Zechariah and for Meshullam, heads, and for Joiarib and for Elnathan, men of understanding.

en.L: And I sent for Eliezer, for Ariel, for Shemaiah, and for Elnathan and for Jarib and for Elnathan and for Nathan and for Zechariah and for Meshullam, leaders, and for Joiarib and for Elnathan, men of understanding.
en.B: So I sent for Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah and Meshullam, who were leaders, and for Joiarib and Elnathan, who were teachers.
en.R: So I sent for some of the leaders: Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah and Meshullam. I also sent for Joiarib and Elnathan, who were teachers.

decisions.choice: men of understanding: teachers, men able to explain the law
decisions.reason: The word describes those who understand and help others understand; it is used of the Levites who taught the people the law (Nehemiah 8:7, 9) and of skilled musicians who trained others (1 Chronicles 25:8).

decisions.choice: Elnathan three times
decisions.reason: The name appears three times in the list. It was a common name, so three men may have borne it; it is also possible that a copyist repeated the name. The Hebrew text is translated as it stands.

decisions.choice: teachers (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what these men were known for; Literal keeps "men of understanding".

source.text: וָאֲצַוֶּ֤ה אוֹתָם֙ עַל־אִדּ֣וֹ הָרֹ֔אשׁ בְּכָסִפְיָ֖א הַמָּק֑וֹם וָאָשִׂימָה֩ בְּפִיהֶ֨ם דְּבָרִ֜ים לְ֠דַבֵּר אֶל־אִדּ֨וֹ אָחִ֤יו הַנְּתִינִים֙ בְּכָסִפְיָ֣א הַמָּק֔וֹם לְהָֽבִיא־לָ֥נוּ מְשָׁרְתִ֖ים לְבֵ֥ית אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I commanded them to Iddo the head in Casiphia the place, and I put in their mouth words to speak to Iddo his brother the Nethinim in Casiphia the place, to bring to us ministers for [the] house of our God.

en.L: And I sent them with a command to Iddo, the head at Casiphia the place, and I put in their mouth words to speak to Iddo [and] his brothers, the Nethinim, at Casiphia the place, to bring to us ministers for the house of our God.
en.B: I sent them to Iddo, the leader at the place called Casiphia, and told them what to say to Iddo and his kinsmen, the temple servants at Casiphia, so that they would bring us ministers for the house of our God.
en.R: I sent them to Iddo, the leader at a place called Casiphia. I told them what to say to Iddo and his relatives, the temple servants who lived there. They were to ask them to send us men who could serve in the temple of our God.

decisions.choice: I commanded them: the reading in the margin
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text mean "I sent them out"; the traditional reading marked for them is "I commanded them". The translation follows the reading. Either way Ezra sends the men to Iddo with a message.

decisions.choice: Casiphia the place: a settlement of Levites and temple servants, not otherwise known
decisions.reason: Casiphia is named only here. "The place" may simply mark it as a town, or it may mean a holy place where exiled Levites gathered for worship and teaching, since "the place" can be used of a sanctuary (Deuteronomy 12:5). Its leader, Iddo, could supply Levites and temple servants.

decisions.choice: Iddo his brother the Nethinim: Iddo and his kinsmen, the temple servants
alternatives: to Iddo's kinsmen, the temple servants
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "Iddo his brother the Nethinim", with no "and". It is most likely to be read "Iddo and his kinsmen, the temple servants", which agrees with what they sent (verses 18-20). Some read "Iddo's kinsmen, the temple servants", leaving Iddo himself out of the phrase.

decisions.choice: ministers: those who serve in the temple's worship
decisions.reason: The word is used of priests and Levites who serve before God (Numbers 3:6; 1 Chronicles 16:4). Here it means Levites.

source.text: וַיָּבִ֨יאּוּ לָ֜נוּ כְּיַד־אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ הַטּוֹבָ֤ה עָלֵ֨ינוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ שֶׂ֔כֶל מִבְּנֵ֣י מַחְלִ֔י בֶּן־לֵוִ֖י בֶּן־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְשֵׁרֵֽבְיָ֛ה וּבָנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁמֹנָ֥ה עָשָֽׂר׃

records.literal_gloss: And they brought to us, according to [the] hand of our God, the good, upon us, a man of insight from [the] sons of Mahli son of Levi son of Israel, and Sherebiah and his sons and his brothers, eighteen,

en.L: And according to the good hand of our God upon us, they brought us a man of insight from the sons of Mahli, the son of Levi, the son of Israel, and Sherebiah and his sons and his brothers, eighteen,
en.B: Because the good hand of our God was on us, they brought us a man of insight, Sherebiah, from the descendants of Mahli son of Levi, son of Israel, together with his sons and his kinsmen, eighteen men,
en.R: Our God was kind to us and helped us, so they sent us a wise man named Sherebiah, a descendant of Mahli son of Levi, son of Israel. Sherebiah came with his sons and his relatives, eighteen men in all.

decisions.choice: a man of insight ... and Sherebiah: most likely Sherebiah himself is the man of insight
alternatives: two men: a man of insight, and Sherebiah
decisions.reason: The "and" before Sherebiah can introduce the name of the man just described ("namely Sherebiah"). Sherebiah later appears as a leading Levite who helps teach the law (8:24; Nehemiah 8:7; 9:4-5). Some read two men, an unnamed man of insight and Sherebiah; others take the words for "man of insight" as a name.

decisions.choice: Mahli son of Levi: a Levite clan
decisions.reason: Mahli was a son of Merari son of Levi (Exodus 6:19; 1 Chronicles 6:4), so "son" here means descendant. The line runs back to Israel, that is, Jacob.

decisions.choice: the good hand of our God upon us
decisions.reason: The refrain of 7:6, 9, 28: Ezra sees God's help in the answer to his request.

source.text: וְאֶת־חֲשַׁבְיָ֔ה וְאִתּ֥וֹ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֖ה מִבְּנֵ֣י מְרָרִ֑י אֶחָ֥יו וּבְנֵיהֶ֖ם עֶשְׂרִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: and Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah of [the] sons of Merari, his brothers and their sons, twenty,

en.L: and Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah of the sons of Merari, his brothers and their sons, twenty,
en.B: and Hashabiah, together with Jeshaiah of the descendants of Merari, with his kinsmen and their sons, twenty men,
en.R: They also sent Hashabiah and Jeshaiah, from the family of Merari, with their relatives and their sons, twenty men in all.

decisions.choice: Hashabiah and Merari
decisions.reason: Hashabiah appears again with Sherebiah in verse 24. Merari was one of the three sons of Levi (Exodus 6:16), the clan to which Mahli also belonged.

source.text: וּמִן־הַנְּתִינִ֗ים שֶׁנָּתַ֨ן דָּוִ֤יד וְהַשָּׂרִים֙ לַעֲבֹדַ֣ת הַלְוִיִּ֔ם נְתִינִ֖ים מָאתַ֣יִם וְעֶשְׂרִ֑ים כֻּלָּ֖ם נִקְּב֥וּ בְשֵׁמֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: and of the Nethinim, whom had given David and the officials for [the] service of the Levites, Nethinim two hundred and twenty; all of them were designated by names.

en.L: and of the Nethinim, whom David and the princes had given for the service of the Levites, 220 Nethinim; all of them were designated by name.
en.B: and also 220 of the temple servants whom David and the officials had given to assist the Levites. All of them were listed by name.
en.R: They also sent 220 temple servants. Long ago David and his leaders had given this group the work of helping the Levites. Each of these men was listed by name.

decisions.choice: whom David and the officials had given: an old royal gift of servants to the temple
decisions.reason: The word for temple servants means "those given". This verse says David and his officials first gave them to help the Levites; the Old Testament does not otherwise record when this happened (compare Joshua 9:27; 1 Chronicles 9:2).

decisions.choice: designated by name: each was registered by name
decisions.reason: Their names were written down, so each could be accounted for, though Ezra does not list them.

decisions.choice: princes (Literal); officials (Balanced); leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word for royal officials is rendered as elsewhere in the book.

source.text: וָאֶקְרָ֨א שָׁ֥ם צוֹם֙ עַל־הַנָּהָ֣ר אַהֲוָ֔א לְהִתְעַנּ֖וֹת לִפְנֵ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ לְבַקֵּ֤שׁ מִמֶּ֨נּוּ֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יְשָׁרָ֔ה לָ֥נוּ וּלְטַפֵּ֖נוּ וּלְכָל־רְכוּשֵֽׁנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I proclaimed there a fast at the river Ahava, to humble ourselves before our God, to seek from him a straight way for us and for our little ones and for all our goods.

en.L: And I proclaimed a fast there, at the river Ahava, that we might humble ourselves before our God, to seek from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a straight way for us and for our little ones and for all our goods.
en.B: Then I proclaimed a fast there by the Ahava canal, so that we might humble ourselves before our God and ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for a safe journey for us, our children and all our possessions.
en.R: There by the Ahava canal I told everyone to fast and go without food. We did this to show that we were humble before our God, and to ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to keep us, our children and everything we owned safe on the journey.

decisions.choice: a fast, to humble ourselves: going without food as a sign of dependence on God
decisions.reason: The verb means to make oneself low, the language used for fasting on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:29, 31). Fasting went with prayer when God's people faced danger (2 Chronicles 20:3; Esther 4:16).

decisions.choice: a straight way: a safe and smooth journey
decisions.reason: A straight or level road is one without obstacles or danger (Psalm 5:9; Isaiah 40:3). The journey was long and the company carried great wealth (verses 26-27).

decisions.choice: our little ones: our children
decisions.reason: The word covers young children and others who cannot look after themselves. Whole families were making the journey.

decisions.choice: fast and go without food
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a fast is for new readers.

source.text: כִּ֣י בֹ֗שְׁתִּי לִשְׁא֤וֹל מִן־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ חַ֣יִל וּפָרָשִׁ֔ים לְעָזְרֵ֥נוּ מֵאוֹיֵ֖ב בַּדָּ֑רֶךְ כִּֽי־אָמַ֨רְנוּ לַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לֵאמֹ֗ר יַד־אֱלֹהֵ֤ינוּ עַל־כָּל־מְבַקְשָׁיו֙ לְטוֹבָ֔ה וְעֻזּ֣וֹ וְאַפּ֔וֹ עַ֖ל כָּל־עֹזְבָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: For I was ashamed to ask from the king a force and horsemen to help us against [the] enemy on the way, for we had said to the king, saying, [The] hand of our God [is] on all who seek him for good, and his strength and his anger [are] on all who forsake him.

en.L: For I was ashamed to ask the king for a force and horsemen to help us against the enemy on the way, because we had said to the king, "The hand of our God is on all who seek {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for good, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger are against all who forsake {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.B: I was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers and horsemen to protect us from enemies on the road, since we had told the king, "The hand of our God is on all who seek {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, for their good, but {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger are against all who forsake {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.R: I was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers and horsemen to protect us from enemies along the way. We had already told the king, "Our God takes care of everyone who looks to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is powerful, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is angry with everyone who turns away from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

decisions.choice: I was ashamed: asking for soldiers would have contradicted what Ezra had said about God
decisions.reason: Ezra had told the king that God protects those who seek him. To ask then for an armed escort would have seemed to doubt it before the king. This was Ezra's choice, not a rule: Nehemiah travelled with army officers and horsemen given by the king (Nehemiah 2:9).

decisions.choice: for good: the hand of God is on those who seek him, for their good
decisions.reason: "For good" describes how God's hand acts on those who seek him, in contrast with his power and anger against those who forsake him (compare 7:9).

decisions.choice: seek him / forsake him: turning to God, or turning away from him
decisions.reason: To seek God is to turn to him in worship, prayer and obedience (2 Chronicles 15:2); to forsake him is to abandon him. The same pair frames God's promise and warning in 2 Chronicles 15:2.

decisions.choice: Our God takes care of everyone who looks to him (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of God's hand and of seeking him in plain words.

source.text: וַנָּצ֛וּמָה וַנְּבַקְשָׁ֥ה מֵאֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ עַל־זֹ֑את וַיֵּעָתֵ֖ר לָֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And we fasted and sought from our God about this, and he let himself be entreated by us.

en.L: And we fasted and sought our God about this, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} let {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} be entreated by us.
en.B: So we fasted and prayed to our God about this, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} listened to our prayer.
en.R: So we went without food and prayed to our God about this, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered our prayer.

decisions.choice: he let himself be entreated: he granted our request
decisions.reason: The verb means to be moved by prayer and to answer it (2 Samuel 24:25; 2 Chronicles 33:13). Ezra writes knowing that the journey ended safely (verse 31).

decisions.choice: prayed; listened to / answered our prayer (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Sought our God" here means asking him in prayer, and "was entreated" is an old word; Balanced and Readable say it plainly.

source.text: וָאַבְדִּ֛ילָה מִשָּׂרֵ֥י הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים שְׁנֵ֣ים עָשָׂ֑ר לְשֵׁרֵֽבְיָ֣ה חֲשַׁבְיָ֔ה וְעִמָּהֶ֥ם מֵאֲחֵיהֶ֖ם עֲשָׂרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I set apart of [the] leaders of the priests twelve, to Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and with them of their brothers ten.

en.L: And I set apart twelve of the leaders of the priests, [and] Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and with them ten of their brothers.
en.B: Then I set apart twelve of the leading priests, together with Sherebiah, Hashabiah and ten of their kinsmen.
en.R: Then I chose twelve of the leading priests, and also twelve Levites: Sherebiah, Hashabiah and ten of their relatives.

decisions.choice: twelve priests, and Sherebiah, Hashabiah and ten others: twelve priests and twelve Levites
alternatives: twelve leading priests, namely Sherebiah, Hashabiah and ten of their kinsmen
decisions.reason: The small word before Sherebiah can mean "to" or mark a further group ("and also"). Sherebiah and Hashabiah are Levites (verses 18-19), and verse 30 says that priests and Levites received the treasure, so Ezra most likely chose twelve priests and twelve Levites. Read the other way, Sherebiah and Hashabiah would be counted among the twelve priests.

decisions.choice: twelve: one for each tribe
decisions.reason: The number matches the twelve tribes of Israel, as do the offerings of verse 35.

decisions.choice: twelve Levites
decisions.reason: Readable makes the reading of the first meaning decision explicit by adding the total and naming them Levites.

source.text: וָאֶשְׁקֳלָ֣הלָהֶ֔ם אֶת־הַכֶּ֥סֶף וְאֶת־הַזָּהָ֖ב וְאֶת־הַכֵּלִ֑ים תְּרוּמַ֣ת בֵּית־אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ הַהֵרִ֨ימוּ֙ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ וְיֹעֲצָ֣יו וְשָׂרָ֔יו וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הַנִּמְצָאִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And I weighed out to them the silver and the gold and the vessels, [the] contribution of [the] house of our God which had offered the king and his counselors and his officials and all Israel who were found.

en.L: And I weighed out to them the silver and the gold and the vessels, the contribution for the house of our God, which the king and his counselors and his princes and all Israel who were present had offered.
en.B: I weighed out to them the silver, the gold and the vessels, the contribution for the house of our God that the king, his counselors, his officials and all the Israelites there had given.
en.R: I weighed the silver, the gold and the bowls and other objects, and gave them to these men. These were the gifts for the temple of our God from the king, his advisers, his leaders, and all the Israelites who lived there.

decisions.choice: contribution: a gift set apart for holy use
decisions.reason: The word is used for gifts lifted out of one's goods and given to God's house (Exodus 25:2-3; Numbers 18:8).

decisions.choice: all Israel who were found there: the Israelites living in Babylonia
decisions.reason: Many Israelites stayed in Babylonia but sent gifts with those who went, as at the first return (1:4, 6; 7:16).

decisions.choice: princes (Literal); officials (Balanced); leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word for the king's high officials is rendered as elsewhere in the book.

source.text: וָאֶשְׁקֲלָ֨ה עַל־יָדָ֜ם כֶּ֗סֶף כִּכָּרִים֙ שֵֽׁשׁ־מֵא֣וֹת וַחֲמִשִּׁ֔ים וּכְלֵי־כֶ֥סֶף מֵאָ֖ה לְכִכָּרִ֑ים זָהָ֖ב מֵאָ֥ה כִכָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And I weighed out into their hand silver, talents six hundred and fifty, and vessels of silver of a hundred talents, gold a hundred talents,

en.L: And I weighed out into their hand 650 talents of silver, and silver vessels of 100 talents, [and] 100 talents of gold,
en.B: I weighed out into their hands {{units:about 24 tons of silver|650 talents of silver}}, silver vessels weighing {{units:about 3 3/4 tons|100 talents}}, {{units:about 3 3/4 tons of gold|100 talents of gold}},
en.R: I weighed out and gave them {{units:about 24 tons of silver|650 talents of silver}}, silver objects weighing {{units:about 3 3/4 tons|100 talents}}, and {{units:about 3 3/4 tons of gold|100 talents of gold}}.

decisions.choice: silver vessels of 100 talents: vessels weighing 100 talents in all
alternatives: 100 silver vessels, worth [a number of] talents
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "vessels of silver of a hundred, of talents". It most likely gives their total weight. Some think a number has dropped out and read "100 silver vessels worth so many talents".

decisions.choice: talents: very large weights of silver and gold
decisions.reason: A talent was about 75 pounds. The totals show how much the king, his court and the Jews of Babylonia gave, and why Ezra was concerned for a safe journey (verse 22).

decisions.choice: modern weights, with talents as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the weights in modern terms through the units setting (650 talents is about 48,750 pounds); Literal keeps the talent.

source.text: וּכְפֹרֵ֤י זָהָב֙ עֶשְׂרִ֔ים לַאֲדַרְכֹנִ֖ים אָ֑לֶף וּכְלֵ֨י נְחֹ֜שֶׁת מֻצְהָ֤ב טוֹבָה֙ שְׁנַ֔יִם חֲמוּדֹ֖ת כַּזָּהָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: and bowls of gold twenty, of darics a thousand, and vessels of bronze, gleaming, fine, two, precious as gold.

en.L: and twenty bowls of gold, of 1,000 darics, and two vessels of fine gleaming bronze, precious as gold.
en.B: and twenty gold bowls worth 1,000 darics, and two vessels of fine polished bronze, as precious as gold.
en.R: They also received twenty gold bowls worth 1,000 darics, and two fine objects of shiny bronze that were as valuable as gold.

decisions.choice: darics: Persian gold coins
decisions.reason: The daric was the gold coin of the Persian kings, first struck under Darius I. It stays "darics" at every level (compare 2:69). The bowls together were worth, or weighed, a thousand of them.

decisions.choice: gleaming fine bronze: bronze of high quality, polished to a shine
decisions.reason: The first word is rare and means shining or golden in color; the second means good or fine. The bronze was valued as highly as gold.

source.text: וָאֹמְרָ֣ה אֲלֵהֶ֗ם אַתֶּ֥ם קֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ לַיהוָ֔ה וְהַכֵּלִ֖ים קֹ֑דֶשׁ וְהַכֶּ֤סֶף וְהַזָּהָב֙ נְדָבָ֔ה לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבֹתֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I said to them, You [are] holy to YHWH, and the vessels [are] holy, and the silver and the gold [are] a freewill offering to YHWH [the] God of your fathers.

en.L: And I said to them, "You are holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the vessels are holy, and the silver and the gold are a freewill offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your fathers.
en.B: And I said to them, "You are holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the vessels are holy. The silver and the gold are a freewill offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your ancestors.
en.R: I told them, "You are set apart as holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and so are these objects. The silver and gold are a gift freely given to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your ancestors.

decisions.choice: you are holy, and the vessels are holy: holy things in the care of holy people
decisions.reason: Priests and Levites were set apart for God's service, and only they could handle the holy objects of the sanctuary (Numbers 4:15; 18:3). Ezra entrusts God's property to those whom God has set apart.

decisions.choice: a freewill offering: a gift beyond what the law requires
decisions.reason: See 7:16. The silver and gold were given freely and now belong to God.

decisions.choice: set apart as holy
decisions.reason: Readable adds "set apart" to say what being holy to the LORD means here.

source.text: שִׁקְד֣וּ וְשִׁמְר֗וּ עַֽד־תִּשְׁקְל֡וּ לִפְנֵי֩ שָׂרֵ֨י הַכֹּהֲנִ֧ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֛ם וְשָׂרֵֽי־הָאָב֥וֹת לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם הַלִּשְׁכ֖וֹת בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Watch and keep [them] until you weigh [them] out before [the] leaders of the priests and the Levites and [the] leaders of the fathers of Israel in Jerusalem, the chambers of [the] house of YHWH.

en.L: Watch and keep them until you weigh them out before the leaders of the priests and the Levites and the leaders of the fathers' [houses] of Israel in Jerusalem, in the chambers of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: Guard them carefully until you weigh them out before the leading priests and Levites and the heads of the families of Israel in Jerusalem, in the storerooms of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.R: Guard them well until you weigh them in front of the leaders of the priests and Levites and the heads of the families of Israel. You will do this in Jerusalem, in the storerooms of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: watch and keep: guard closely
decisions.reason: The two verbs together stress careful watching over a charge.

decisions.choice: the chambers: storerooms in the temple courts
decisions.reason: Rooms around the temple courts held the gifts, tithes and holy objects (Nehemiah 10:38-40; 13:4-9).

decisions.choice: the leaders of the fathers: the heads of the ancestral families
decisions.reason: As in 8:1, "fathers" stands for the fathers' houses, the extended families.

source.text: וְקִבְּלוּ֙ הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֔ם מִשְׁקַ֛ל הַכֶּ֥סֶף וְהַזָּהָ֖ב וְהַכֵּלִ֑ים לְהָבִ֥יא לִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם לְבֵ֥ית אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And took the priests and the Levites [the] weight of the silver and the gold and the vessels, to bring [them] to Jerusalem to [the] house of our God.

en.L: And the priests and the Levites received the weight of the silver and the gold and the vessels, to bring them to Jerusalem to the house of our God.
en.B: So the priests and the Levites took charge of the silver, gold and vessels that had been weighed out, to bring them to Jerusalem to the house of our God.
en.R: So the priests and Levites took the silver, gold and other objects that had been weighed. They were to bring them to the temple of our God in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: received the weight: took responsibility for the weighed amount
decisions.reason: They took charge of the treasure by its recorded weight and would answer for it in Jerusalem (verses 33-34).

source.text: וַֽנִּסְעָ֞ה מִנְּהַ֣ר אַֽהֲוָ֗א בִּשְׁנֵ֤ים עָשָׂר֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֔וֹן לָלֶ֖כֶת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְיַד־אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ הָיְתָ֣ה עָלֵ֔ינוּ וַיַּ֨צִּילֵ֔נוּ מִכַּ֥ף אוֹיֵ֛ב וְאוֹרֵ֖ב עַל־הַדָּֽרֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And we set out from [the] river Ahava on [the] twelfth of the first month to go [to] Jerusalem, and [the] hand of our God was upon us, and he delivered us from [the] palm of [the] enemy and ambusher on the way.

en.L: And we set out from the river Ahava on the twelfth [day] of the first month to go to Jerusalem; and the hand of our God was upon us, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} delivered us from the hand of the enemy and the ambusher on the way.
en.B: On the twelfth day of the first month we set out from the Ahava canal to go to Jerusalem. The hand of our God was on us, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rescued us from enemies and from ambushes along the way.
en.R: We left the Ahava canal on the twelfth day of the first month and started for Jerusalem. Our God was with us, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} kept us safe from enemies and from robbers who hid along the road to attack us.

decisions.choice: the twelfth of the first month: the day the company left Ahava
decisions.reason: The departure had been set for the first day (7:9); the three days' camp, the search for Levites and the fast came between. The journey to Jerusalem took until the first day of the fifth month (7:9).

decisions.choice: from the palm of the enemy and ambusher: from the power of enemies and of those who lay in wait
decisions.reason: The "palm" or hand means power. The second word is one who lies in ambush, such as raiders on the desert roads. Ezra's trust (verse 22) was answered.

decisions.choice: robbers who hid along the road to attack us (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "ambusher" with a familiar picture.

source.text: וַנָּב֖וֹא יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַנֵּ֥שֶׁב שָׁ֖ם יָמִ֥ים שְׁלֹשָֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And we came [to] Jerusalem and we stayed there days three.

en.L: And we came to Jerusalem, and we stayed there three days.
en.B: We arrived in Jerusalem and stayed there three days.
en.R: When we arrived in Jerusalem, we rested for three days.

decisions.choice: we stayed: we remained, resting after the journey
decisions.reason: The verb means to sit or stay. After four months on the road the company rested before handing over the treasure, as Nehemiah also waited three days (Nehemiah 2:11).

decisions.choice: rested (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says why they stayed without doing anything for three days.

source.text: וּבַיּ֣וֹם הָרְבִיעִ֡י נִשְׁקַ֣ל הַכֶּסֶף֩ וְהַזָּהָ֨ב וְהַכֵּלִ֜ים בְּבֵ֣ית אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ עַ֠ל יַד־מְרֵמ֤וֹת בֶּן־אֽוּרִיָּה֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְעִמּ֖וֹ אֶלְעָזָ֣ר בֶּן־פִּֽינְחָ֑ס וְעִמָּהֶ֞ם יוֹזָבָ֧ד בֶּן־יֵשׁ֛וּעַ וְנֽוֹעַדְיָ֥ה בֶן־בִּנּ֖וּי הַלְוִיִּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And on the day the fourth was weighed out the silver and the gold and the vessels in [the] house of our God into [the] hand of Meremoth son of Uriah the priest, and with him Eleazar son of Phinehas, and with them Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui, the Levites,

en.L: And on the fourth day the silver and the gold and the vessels were weighed out in the house of our God into the hand of Meremoth the son of Uriah the priest, and with him was Eleazar the son of Phinehas, and with them were Jozabad the son of Jeshua and Noadiah the son of Binnui, the Levites,
en.B: On the fourth day, in the house of our God, the silver, the gold and the vessels were weighed out into the hands of Meremoth son of Uriah, the priest. With him were Eleazar son of Phinehas and the Levites Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui,
en.R: On the fourth day, in the temple of our God, the silver, gold and other objects were weighed and handed over to Meremoth the priest, the son of Uriah. With him were Eleazar son of Phinehas and two Levites, Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui.

decisions.choice: Meremoth son of Uriah the priest: a priest in charge of the temple treasury
decisions.reason: "The priest" most likely describes Meremoth, who received the treasure. A Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, repaired two sections of the wall in Nehemiah's day (Nehemiah 3:4, 21). The family of Hakkoz had been unable to prove its priestly descent (2:61-62); if this is the same family, it had by now been restored to service.

decisions.choice: Eleazar son of Phinehas: a priest of Ezra's day
decisions.reason: Not the Eleazar and Phinehas of Moses' time (7:5); the names were common in priestly families.

decisions.choice: the fourth day: after three days' rest
decisions.reason: The handing over took place on the day after the rest of verse 32.

decisions.choice: Meremoth the priest, the son of Uriah (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable places "the priest" next to Meremoth, following the reading of the first meaning decision; Balanced keeps the Hebrew order.

source.text: בְּמִסְפָּ֥ר בְּמִשְׁקָ֖ל לַכֹּ֑ל וַיִּכָּתֵ֥ב כָּֽל־הַמִּשְׁקָ֖ל בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִֽיא׃פ

records.literal_gloss: by number, by weight, for everything; and was written down all the weight at that time.

en.L: by number [and] by weight for everything; and all the weight was written down at that time.
en.B: everything by number and by weight, and the total weight was recorded at that time.
en.R: Everything was counted and weighed, and the total weight was written down at that time.

decisions.choice: by number and by weight: everything checked against the record made at Ahava
decisions.reason: Each item was counted and weighed, and the total was written down. Nothing had been lost on the journey, as the king had ordered (7:19) and as Ezra had charged the priests (8:29).

source.text: הַ֠בָּאִים מֵֽהַשְּׁבִ֨י בְנֵֽי־הַגּוֹלָ֜ה הִקְרִ֥יבוּ עֹל֣וֹת׀לֵאלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל פָּרִ֨ים שְׁנֵים־עָשָׂ֤ר עַל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֵילִ֣ים׀תִּשְׁעִ֣ים וְשִׁשָּׁ֗ה כְּבָשִׂים֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים וְשִׁבְעָ֔ה צְפִירֵ֥י חַטָּ֖את שְׁנֵ֣ים עָשָׂ֑ר הַכֹּ֖ל עוֹלָ֥ה לַיהוָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Those coming from the captivity, [the] sons of the exile, offered burnt offerings to [the] God of Israel: bulls twelve for all Israel, rams ninety-six, lambs seventy-seven, male goats [of] sin offering twelve; all [was] a burnt offering to YHWH.

en.L: Those who had come from the captivity, the sons of the exile, offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, [and] twelve male goats [as] a sin offering; all [of it was] a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: The returned exiles who had come from captivity offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve male goats as a sin offering. All this was a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Then the people who came back from exile offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel. They offered twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve male goats as a sin offering. All of this was a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the sons of the exile: the exiles who had returned
decisions.reason: The phrase is the book's name for the community that came back from Babylon (4:1; 6:19-21). Here it means Ezra's company, "those who had come from the captivity".

decisions.choice: twelve bulls for all Israel: offerings for the whole people
decisions.reason: The numbers are built on twelve, the number of the tribes: twelve bulls, ninety-six rams (eight times twelve), twelve goats. As at the temple's dedication (6:17), the returned exiles offer for all Israel, not only for Judah.

decisions.choice: all was a burnt offering: a summary of the whole sacrifice
decisions.reason: The goats were a sin offering, which was not wholly burned (Leviticus 6:17-23 in the Hebrew numbering). "All was a burnt offering" sums up the sacrifices as given to the LORD; it does not change the goats into burnt offerings.

decisions.choice: the returned exiles (Balanced); the people who came back from exile (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book's wording for this phrase; Literal keeps "the sons of the exile".

source.text: וַֽיִּתְּנ֣וּ׀אֶת־דָּתֵ֣י הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ לַאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנֵי֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וּפַחֲו֖וֹת עֵ֣בֶר הַנָּהָ֑ר וְנִשְּׂא֥וּ אֶת־הָעָ֖ם וְאֶת־בֵּֽית־הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they gave the decrees of the king to [the] satraps of the king and [the] governors of Beyond the River, and they supported the people and [the] house of God.

en.L: And they delivered the decrees of the king to the satraps of the king and the governors of Beyond the River, and they supported the people and the house of God.
en.B: They also delivered the king's orders to the royal satraps and to the governors of the province Beyond the River, who then gave their support to the people and to the house of God.
en.R: They also gave the king's orders to the king's regional governors and to the officials who governed the province west of the Euphrates. These officials then helped the people and supported God's temple.

decisions.choice: satraps and governors: the empire's regional rulers and the local governors under them
decisions.reason: Satraps ruled the great divisions of the Persian empire; governors ruled the smaller provinces within them, such as Judah. They received the king's decree of 7:21-24.

decisions.choice: they supported: the officials aided the people and the temple
decisions.reason: The subject changes: the first "they" is Ezra's company, the second is the officials, who now gave the help the king had ordered. The verb means to lift up or to support.

decisions.choice: the decrees of the king: the royal orders
decisions.reason: The word is a Persian loanword for a law or decree, used of the king's letter (7:12-26).

decisions.choice: regional governors (Readable); satraps (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "satraps", as the Esther chapters do.
